narrative:
The model estimates a 52% chance that you will leave your current job, which is just over the threshold for predicting departure. As a result, the organization has decided to deny your promotion.

The prediction is driven primarily by three key aspects of your profile. First, having only 1-5 years of total professional experience across all roles was the strongest factor pulling the prediction toward leaving. Among employees the model expected to stay, only about half had similarly short overall experience, while many had 6-10 years or more; the model sees longer cumulative experience as a strong anchor that keeps people in their jobs.

Second, the fact that you have not received other job offers while working here also pushed the prediction toward departure. This absence of external opportunities appears, counter-intuitively, to signal lower attachment in the eyes of the model.

Third, finding it difficult to get involved in decision-making and having your opinions heard at work was the factor that most strongly pushed the prediction in the opposite direction, toward staying. However, this positive influence was not large enough to outweigh the first two effects.

The organization should consider discussing your limited overall experience and lack of involvement in decisions with you openly. You may want to explore ways to gain broader experience or seek roles that offer greater voice in how work gets done. These steps could improve both your satisfaction and your future promotion prospects. (248 words)
